slots.title: The dark
slots.text: …I stood upon the edge of the abyss. The cold bit at my skin as the dark mist swelled around me and overhead. I stared into the darkness, straining my eyes to glimpse something… anything. I stayed motionless for some time, praying that I might see some sign of hope, but no. For in the great darkness, no light can be found…

interpretation.text: This is a place Elaris has stood: the dark of a book he would not leave.

slots.title: The vow
slots.text: "Elaris Sel Marden, reader of the third gallery. Bound as keeper on the day of Keeper Maudric's death. Until his own."

slots.carrier: A folded letter from another reader
slots.title: The cost
slots.text: He read the Lantern Country as its narrator for a season, and would not set the cup down. While he stayed, its story could not end, and its lamps burned down one by one. "They are all in the dark now."

slots.carrier: The Wardens of the Shelves' ruling, strap-bound
slots.title: The judgment
slots.text: The sentence: to be shelved inside the dark book, reading forever into a world with no light.

slots.fragment: Why it was better than deserved
slots.title: The mercy
slots.text: "Let him keep them all, since he could not keep one." Maudric asked for this as he was dying.

slots.title: What remains
slots.text: The Lantern Country, cold to the touch, mist at its edges, on the unlit shelf.

slots.carrier: A voice in the dark, remembered
slots.title: A name
slots.text: Wenna, the lamp-keeper's daughter, who asked him to let the story end, and who kept a list of the names of the stars. One star name comes back to him.

voice_line.text: That one is called the Thread. That one, the Ewe.
